_about: Fourteen backgrounds in five groups. Each grants at most two points of skill in the
`background` bonus type - so two backgrounds cannot stack and a trait can still be
taken beside one - and each carries at least one *tie*, which is the point of the
whole thing: a slot filled from this world at creation, so the history names
No background grants a combat number. 1e has no background system, and the moment
one gives an attack or a save bonus it is competing with feats, which are priced.
What these grant instead is standing: people who know you, places you can walk
into, and things you are assumed to know - every one of them a `knows.*` tag the
narrator's brief may state as true and a quest scheme can open on.

backgrounds.name: Apprenticed
backgrounds.summary: You were bound to a craft before you were bound to anything else.
traits: You can tell good work from work that was hurried.
Somebody taught you, and has opinions about how you turned out.

ties.says: You were apprenticed to $who at $where, and left on terms you can live with.

backgrounds.name: Stallholder
backgrounds.summary: You have stood behind a table and sold things to people who did not want them.
traits: You know what a thing is worth and what it can be got for, which are two numbers.
You have been cheated exactly once.

ties.says: You kept a pitch at $where and the neighbours still nod.

backgrounds.name: Caravan hand
backgrounds.summary: You walked beside other people's goods for a living.
traits: You know which roads are worth the tolls and which are worth the risk.
You have slept rough more nights than not.

ties.says: You have come and gone by $where more times than you can count.

backgrounds.name: Gate watch
backgrounds.summary: You stood at a gate and decided who came in.
traits: You know what the watch will and will not do about a thing.
You have turned somebody away who should have been let in.

ties.says: You stood the watch at $where under $who, who remembers you.

backgrounds.name: Thief-taker
backgrounds.summary: You were paid per body, and the pay was never the point.
traits: You know how a person moves when they are about to run.
Somebody you brought in is out again.

ties.says: $who used to pay you by the name, and has not stopped asking.

backgrounds.name: Exile
backgrounds.summary: You are not from here and cannot go back to where you are from.
traits: You have learned how to arrive somewhere and not be a problem.
There is a place you will not talk about.

ties.says: You came in by $where with what you could carry.

backgrounds.name: Pilgrim
backgrounds.summary: You set out for a reason and have not finished with it.
traits: You are owed hospitality in places you have never been.
You can tell whether a shrine is tended or only swept.

ties.says: You were given a bed at $where by $who, and it was not charity.

backgrounds.name: Forager
backgrounds.summary: You have fed yourself off ground nobody owns.
traits: You know which of a thing is the part worth taking.
You have eaten something you should not have, once.

ties.says: You have worked the ground out past $where since you were small.

backgrounds.name: In service
backgrounds.summary: You worked in somebody else's house and heard everything said in it.
traits: You know how a household actually runs, which is never how it says it does.
You left, and it was not entirely your idea.

ties.says: You were in the service of $who, and $where is where they put you.

backgrounds.name: Guild clerk
backgrounds.summary: You kept somebody's books and know what was in them.
traits: You can read a ledger for what it is not saying.
There is an entry you did not query and should have.

ties.says: You wrote for $who at $where, and the hand is still recognisable.

backgrounds.name: Innkeeper's child
backgrounds.summary: You grew up where everyone passing through had to stop.
traits: You are good at names and better at knowing who not to seat together.
You have heard more than you have ever repeated.

ties.says: You grew up at $where and the room still quietens when you come in.

backgrounds.name: Bonesetter
backgrounds.summary: People come to you broken and you do what can be done.
traits: You know what a wound will do before it does it.
You have lost somebody you should have been able to keep.

ties.says: You learned it from $who, and were better at it than expected.

backgrounds.name: Pit fighter
backgrounds.summary: You were paid to be hit in front of people.
traits: You know how a crowd turns and how long you have before it does.
Your name is known to people who have never met you.

ties.says: You fought where $who took the bets, near $where, and drew a crowd.

backgrounds.name: Ferryman
backgrounds.summary: You moved people across something that would have killed them.
traits: You know the water here and what it does in each season.
You have pulled somebody out, and not pulled somebody else out.

ties.says: You worked the crossing out past $where and know its moods.
